case_studies.title: SynSur: An end-to-end generative pipeline for synthetic industrial surface defect generation and detection
case_studies.abstract: The bottleneck in learning-based industrial defect detection is often limited not by model capacity, but by the scarcity of labeled defect data: defects are rare, annotations are expensive, and collecting balanced training sets is slow. We present an end-to-end pipeline for synthetic defect generation and annotation, combining Vision-Language-Model-based prompts, LoRA-adapted diffusion, mask-guided inpainting, and sample filtering with automatic label derivation, and demonstrates the potential of real data with realistic synthetic samples to overcome data scarcity. The evaluation is conducted
case_studies.summary: The scarcity of labeled defect data hinders the development of learning-based industrial defect detection systems. To address this, the proposed SynSur pipeline generates synthetic defects using a combination of Vision-Language-Model-based prompts, LoRA-adapted diffusion, and mask-guided inpainting. The evaluation demonstrates the potential of using real data with realistic synthetic samples to overcome data scarcity and improve defect detection accuracy.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the SynSur pipeline by integrating it into their existing defect detection systems, using the generated synthetic defects to augment their training data and improve model performance. Additionally, they can fine-tune the pipeline's parameters to adapt to their specific use cases and defect types.
case_studies.monetisation: The SynSur pipeline presents a concrete business opportunity for companies developing industrial defect detection systems, as it can help reduce the costs and time associated with data collection and annotation. By licensing or integrating the SynSur technology, these companies can improve the accuracy and efficiency of their systems, leading to increased customer satisfaction and revenue growth.

case_studies.title: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Models across XPUs: Constraints and Acceleration for On-Robot Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are promising for generalist robot control, but on-robot deployment is bottlenecked by real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. Most prior evaluations rely on desktop-grade GPUs, obscuring the trade-offs and opportunities offered by heterogeneous edge accelerators (GPUs/XPUs/NPUs). We present a systematic analysis for low-cost VLA deployment via model-hardware co-characterization. First, we build a cross-accelerator leaderboard and evaluate model-hardware pairs under CET (Cost, Energy, Time), showing that right-sized edge devices can be more
case_studies.summary: The problem of deploying Vision-Language-Action models on robots is bottlenecked by real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. The authors' AI approach involves a systematic analysis of model-hardware co-characterization to evaluate low-cost VLA deployment via a cross-accelerator leaderboard. The outcome shows that right-sized edge devices can be more efficient than desktop-grade GPUs, offering opportunities for on-robot deployment.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this research, AI practitioners can use the cross-accelerator leaderboard to evaluate and optimize their own VLA models for deployment on edge devices. By considering the trade-offs between cost, energy, and time, practitioners can make informed decisions about hardware and model selection for on-robot deployment.
case_studies.monetisation: A concrete business opportunity arising from this research is the development of specialized edge devices or software solutions for efficient VLA model deployment on robots. Companies can leverage the findings of this study to create products or services that cater to the growing demand for autonomous robots with advanced vision-language-action capabilities.
case_studies.relevance_tag: AI Agents, Computer Vision, NLP, MLOps

case_studies.title: AgentPulse: A Continuous Multi-Signal Framework for Evaluating AI Agents in Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Static benchmarks measure what AI agents can do at a fixed point in time but not how they are adopted, maintained, or experienced in deployment. We introduce AgentPulse, a continuous evaluation framework scoring 50 agents across 10 workload categories along four factors (Benchmark Performance, Adoption Signals, Community Sentiment, and Ecosystem Health) aggregated from 18 real-time signals across GitHub, package registries, IDE marketplaces, social platforms, and benchmark leaderboards. Three analyses ground the framework. The four factors capture largely complementary information (n=50; $ρ_{\
case_studies.summary: The current static benchmarks for evaluating AI agents have limitations, as they only measure performance at a fixed point in time. The AgentPulse framework addresses this issue by providing a continuous evaluation approach that scores AI agents across multiple factors, including benchmark performance, adoption signals, community sentiment, and ecosystem health. This framework has the potential to improve the assessment and deployment of AI agents in various applications.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from AgentPulse by incorporating continuous evaluation metrics into their agent development and deployment pipelines, allowing for more comprehensive and dynamic assessments of AI performance. By doing so, developers can identify areas for improvement and optimize their agents for real-world deployment scenarios.
case_studies.monetisation: The AgentPulse framework presents a business opportunity for companies to develop and offer continuous evaluation services for AI agents, providing valuable insights for organizations looking to deploy and maintain effective AI systems. This could be achieved through the creation of a software platform or consulting service that leverages the AgentPulse framework to evaluate and improve AI agent performance.

case_studies.title: HalluCiteChecker: A Lightweight Toolkit for Hallucinated Citation Detection and Verification in the Era of AI Scientists
case_studies.abstract: We introduce HalluCiteChecker, a toolkit for detecting and verifying hallucinated citations in scientific papers. While AI assistant technologies have transformed the academic writing process, including citation recommendation, they have also led to the emergence of hallucinated citations that do not correspond to any existing work. Such citations not only undermine the credibility of scientific papers but also impose an additional burden on reviewers and authors, who must manually verify their validity during the review process. In this study, we formalize hallucinated citation detection as a
case_studies.summary: The emergence of hallucinated citations in scientific papers, caused by AI assistant technologies, undermines the credibility of research and imposes a burden on reviewers and authors. HalluCiteChecker, a lightweight toolkit, uses AI to detect and verify hallucinated citations, Formalizing hallucinated citation detection as a distinct problem. The outcome of this study is a potential solution to improve the academic writing process and maintain the integrity of scientific research.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept, AI practitioners can utilize natural language processing and machine learning algorithms to develop tools that detect and verify citations in scientific papers. By leveraging this approach, researchers can automate the citation verification process, reducing the workload on reviewers and authors, and increasing the overall efficiency of the academic publishing process.
case_studies.monetisation: The HalluCiteChecker toolkit presents a concrete business opportunity for companies that provide academic publishing services, as it can be integrated into existing platforms to improve the quality and credibility of published research. By offering this tool as a value-added service, companies can differentiate themselves from competitors and attract more customers, generating revenue and increasing their market share.

case_studies.title: Domain-Adapted Small Language Models for Reliable Clinical Triage
case_studies.abstract: Accurate and consistent Emergency Severity Index (ESI) assignment remains a persistent challenge in emergency departments, where highly variable free-text triage documentation contributes to mistriage and workflow inefficiencies. This study evaluates whether open-source small language models (SLMs) can serve as reliable, privacy-preserving decision-support tools for clinical triage. We systematically compared multiple SLMs across diverse prompting pipelines and found that clinical vignettes, concise summaries of triage narratives, yielded the most accurate predictions. The SLM, Qwen2.5-7B, dem
case_studies.summary: The Emergency Severity Index (ESI) assignment in emergency departments is a challenging task due to variable free-text triage documentation, leading to mistriage and workflow inefficiencies. This study evaluates the use of open-source small language models (SLMs) as reliable decision-support tools for clinical triage, finding that clinical vignettes yield the most accurate predictions. The SLM, Qwen2.5-7B, demonstrates promising results in this context, with potential for further development and implementation.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can utilize clinical vignettes as concise summaries of triage narratives to improve the accuracy of SLM predictions, and experiment with diverse prompting pipelines to optimize model performance. By fine-tuning SLMs on specific clinical datasets, practitioners can develop more effective decision-support tools for clinical triage.
case_studies.monetisation: The development of a clinical triage decision-support tool based on SLMs could provide a clear product opportunity, with potential for integration into existing electronic health record systems or as a standalone application for emergency departments. A company could offer this solution as a subscription-based service, providing regular model updates and support to ensure optimal performance and reliability.

case_studies.title: Robustness Evaluation of a Foundation Segmentation Model Under Simulated Domain Shifts in Abdominal CT: Implications for Health Digital Twin Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Foundation segmentation models such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM) have demonstrated strong generalization across natural images; however, their robustness under clinically realistic medical imaging domain shifts remains insufficiently quantified. We present a systematic slice-level robustness audit of SAM (ViT-B) for spleen segmentation in abdominal CT using 1,051 nonempty slices from 41 volumes in the Medical Segmentation Decathlon. A standardized ground-truth-derived bounding-box protocol was used to isolate encoder robustness from prompt uncertainty. Controlled perturbations simulatin
case_studies.summary: The study evaluates the robustness of a foundation segmentation model, specifically the Segment Anything Model (SAM), under simulated domain shifts in abdominal CT images. The AI approach uses a systematic slice-level robustness audit to quantify the model's performance, and the outcome highlights the need for further research to improve the model's robustness in clinically realistic medical imaging scenarios. The results have implications for the deployment of health digital twins, which rely on accurate and robust medical image segmentation.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this research in practice, AI practitioners can use the standardized ground-truth-derived bounding-box protocol to evaluate the robustness of their own segmentation models, and consider using controlled perturbations to simulate real-world domain shifts. By doing so, they can identify potential weaknesses in their models and develop strategies to improve their performance in diverse and dynamic environments.
case_studies.monetisation: The research has a clear potential for monetisation in the healthcare industry, where accurate and robust medical image segmentation can improve patient outcomes and reduce costs. For example, a company could develop a product that uses the evaluated segmentation model to provide automated spleen segmentation in abdominal CT images, and offer it as a service to healthcare providers.

case_studies.title: Feasible-First Exploration for Constrained ML Deployment Optimization in Crash-Prone Hierarchical Search Spaces
case_studies.abstract: Deploying machine learning models under production constraints requires joint optimization over model family, quantization scheme, runtime backend, and serving configuration. This induces a hierarchical mixed-variable search space in which many configurations are invalid: evaluations may crash, exceed memory limits, or violate latency constraints. Standard black-box optimizers such as Tree-structured Parzen Estimators (TPE) and constrained Bayesian optimization are effective when valid configurations are common, but they can spend a large fraction of a small evaluation budget on invalid or uni
case_studies.summary: The problem of deploying machine learning models under production constraints is addressed through a hierarchical mixed-variable search space, which can be prone to crashes and invalid configurations. The proposed AI approach, Feasible-First Exploration, aims to optimize the search space by identifying valid configurations first. The outcome of this approach is a more efficient optimization process, reducing the time spent on invalid configurations and improving the overall deployment of machine learning models.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this approach by prioritizing the identification of valid configurations in their search space, using techniques such as feasibility checks and constraint satisfaction. By doing so, they can reduce the waste of evaluation budget on invalid configurations and improve the efficiency of their optimization process.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed approach can be monetized by offering it as a service to companies that deploy machine learning models, helping them to optimize their deployment process and reduce costs. Additionally, the approach can be integrated into existing MLOps platforms, providing a competitive advantage and increasing the potential for revenue generation.

case_studies.title: Network Impact of Post-Quantum Certificate Chain sizes on Time to First Byte in TLS Deployments
case_studies.abstract: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) is a rapidly growing deployment challenge as cryptographically relevant quantum computers (CRQC) continue to advance, leaving traditional cryptographic algorithms used in X.509 vulnerable to attack. However, PQC introduces significant deployment challenges in real-world networks, with handshake sizes increasing from 5x to over 20x compared to classical algorithms. In this work, we evaluate the time to first byte (TTFB) under CDN-focused TLS conditions to characterize the latency cost of transitioning existing internet infrastructure to quantum-safe certificate s
case_studies.summary: The deployment of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) poses significant challenges in real-world networks due to increased handshake sizes. To address this, the authors evaluate the time to first byte (TTFB) under CDN-focused TLS conditions to characterize the latency cost of transitioning to quantum-safe certificates. The study provides valuable insights into the network impact of PQC certificate chain sizes on TTFB in TLS deployments.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the findings of this study, AI practitioners can focus on optimizing the performance of PQC-based TLS deployments by minimizing the latency cost of larger certificate chain sizes. This can be achieved by leveraging techniques such as certificate compression, parallel processing, and optimized network protocols.
case_studies.monetisation: The study's findings present a clear business opportunity for companies specializing in network security and optimization, as they can develop and market solutions to mitigate the latency costs associated with PQC deployments. By providing optimized PQC-based TLS solutions, these companies can help organizations ensure a seamless transition to quantum-safe certificates while minimizing the impact on their network performance.

case_studies.title: SecMate: Multi-Agent Adaptive Cybersecurity Troubleshooting with Tri-Context Personalization
case_studies.abstract: Recent advances in large language models and agentic frameworks have enabled virtual customer assistants (VCAs) for complex support. We present SecMate, a multi-agent VCA for cybersecurity troubleshooting that integrates device, user, and service specificity from conversational and device-level signals. Device specificity is provided by a lightweight local diagnostic utility, while user specificity relies on implicit proficiency inference and profile-aware troubleshooting. Service specificity is achieved through a proactive, context-aware recommender. We evaluate SecMate in a controlled study
case_studies.summary: The problem of cybersecurity troubleshooting is complex and requires personalized solutions. SecMate, a multi-agent virtual customer assistant, utilizes large language models and agentic frameworks to provide device, user, and service specificity for effective troubleshooting. The outcome of this approach is a more efficient and adaptive cybersecurity support system.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the concept of tri-context personalization to develop more effective virtual customer assistants by integrating device, user, and service specificity. By leveraging conversational and device-level signals, AI models can provide more accurate and tailored support to users.
case_studies.monetisation: SecMate has the potential to be developed into a commercial product, offering customizable cybersecurity troubleshooting solutions to businesses and individuals. The proactive, context-aware recommender system can also be licensed to other companies, providing an additional revenue stream.

case_studies.title: MetaSR: Content-Adaptive Metadata Orchestration for Generative Super-Resolution
case_studies.abstract: We study generative super-resolution (SR) in real-world scenarios where content and degradations vary across domains, genres, and segments. For example, images and videos may alternate between text overlays, fast motion, smooth cartoons, and low-light faces, each benefiting from different forms of side information. Existing metadata-guided SR methods typically use a fixed conditioning design, which is suboptimal when useful cues are content dependent and transmission budgets are limited. We propose MetaSR, a Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based framework that selects and injects task-relevant met
case_studies.summary: The study addresses the challenge of generative super-resolution in real-world scenarios where content and degradations vary, requiring adaptive metadata orchestration. The proposed MetaSR framework utilizes a Diffusion Transformer to select and inject task-relevant metadata, improving super-resolution outcomes. By dynamically adapting to content-dependent cues, MetaSR enhances the effectiveness of super-resolution in diverse applications.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from MetaSR by incorporating adaptive metadata orchestration into their own super-resolution models, particularly in applications with diverse content and degradation types. This can be achieved by exploring the use of Diffusion Transformers and similar architectures to selectively utilize relevant metadata and improve model performance.
case_studies.monetisation: The MetaSR framework presents a clear opportunity for product development in the field of computer vision, particularly in applications such as video enhancement, image restoration, and content creation. Companies can leverage the adaptive metadata orchestration approach to create more effective and efficient super-resolution solutions, potentially leading to new product lines or features that enhance user experience and drive revenue.

case_studies.title: Apriori-based Analysis of Learned Helplessness in Mathematics Tutoring: Behavioral Patterns by Level, Intervention, and Outcome
case_studies.abstract: This study applied the Apriori algorithm to analyze behavioral interaction patterns associated with learned helplessness (LH) in mathematics tutoring system logs. Interaction data were examined across three dimensions: LH level (low vs. high), system-based intervention (with vs. without), and problem-solving outcomes (solved vs. unsolved). The analysis of the complete dataset showed that skipping problems without using hints was the most frequent pattern linked to unsolved outcomes, while persistence behaviors such as not skipping were less dominant overall. Comparisons by LH level showed that
case_studies.summary: The study addresses the problem of learned helplessness in mathematics tutoring by applying the Apriori algorithm to analyze behavioral interaction patterns. The AI approach involves examining interaction data across three dimensions: learned helplessness level, system-based intervention, and problem-solving outcomes. The outcome of the study shows that skipping problems without using hints is the most frequent pattern linked to unsolved outcomes, while persistence behaviors are less dominant overall.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the findings of this study by incorporating Apriori-based analysis into their own tutoring systems to identify patterns of learned helplessness and develop targeted interventions. By analyzing interaction data, practitioners can design more effective tutoring systems that promote persistence and problem-solving skills in students.
case_studies.monetisation: The study's findings can be monetized by developing and marketing a mathematics tutoring system that incorporates Apriori-based analysis and targeted interventions to address learned helplessness. This system could be sold to educational institutions or used as a premium feature in an existing online tutoring platform.

case_studies.title: Exploring the Potential of Probabilistic Transformer for Time Series Modeling: A Report on the ST-PT Framework
case_studies.abstract: The Probabilistic Transformer (PT) establishes that the Transformer's self-attention plus its feed-forward block is mathematically equivalent to Mean-Field Variational Inference (MFVI) on a Conditional Random Field (CRF). Under this equivalence the Transformer ceases to be a black-box neural network and becomes a programmable factor graph: graph topology, factor potentials, and the message-passing schedule are all explicit and inspectable primitives that can be engineered. PT was originally developed for natural language and in this report we investigate its potential for time series. We first
case_studies.summary: The report explores the potential of the Probabilistic Transformer for time series modeling, investigating its applicability beyond natural language processing. The Probabilistic Transformer is mathematically equivalent to Mean-Field Variational Inference on a Conditional Random Field, allowing for explicit and inspectable primitives. This approach can potentially improve time series modeling by providing a more interpretable and programmable model.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can use the Probabilistic Transformer to model time series data by specifying the graph topology, factor potentials, and message-passing schedule. By doing so, they can leverage the benefits of a probabilistic and interpretable model, such as improved performance and explainability.
case_studies.monetisation: The Probabilistic Transformer has the potential to be monetised in industries that rely heavily on time series analysis, such as finance and IoT. Companies can develop products that utilise this approach to provide more accurate and reliable time series forecasting, leading to improved decision-making and revenue growth.

case_studies.title: FutureWorld: A Live Environment for Training Predictive Agents with Real-World Outcome Rewards
case_studies.abstract: Live future prediction refers to the task of making predictions about real-world events before they unfold. This task is increasingly studied using large language model-based agent systems, and it is important for building agents that can continually learn from real-world. Just as interactive environments have often driven progress in agents, advancing live future prediction naturally motivates viewing it as a learning environment. Prior works have explored future prediction from several different parts, but have generally not framed it as a unified learning environment. This task is appealing
case_studies.summary: The problem of live future prediction involves making predictions about real-world events before they unfold, which is increasingly important for building agents that can continually learn from the real-world. The proposed AI approach, FutureWorld, frames live future prediction as a unified learning environment, leveraging large language model-based agent systems. The outcome of this approach is a live environment for training predictive agents with real-world outcome rewards, which has the potential to drive progress in agents.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept, AI practitioners can explore framing their predictive tasks as a unified learning environment, allowing for more effective training of predictive agents. By leveraging large language models and real-world outcome rewards, practitioners can create more accurate and adaptive predictive systems.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed FutureWorld environment has the potential to be monetised as a platform for training and deploying predictive agents, with applications in various industries such as finance and healthcare. Companies can utilise this platform to develop more accurate predictive models, leading to improved decision-making and increased revenue.

case_studies.title: Deep-testing: the case of dependence detection
case_studies.abstract: Deep learning methods have proved highly effective for classification and image recognition problems. In this paper, we ask whether this success can be transferred to hypothesis testing: if a neural network can distinguish, for example, an image of a handwritten digit from another, can it also distinguish an "image of a sample" (such as a scatter plot) generated under a given statistical model from one generated outside that model? Motivated by this idea, we propose a novel procedure called deep-testing, which approaches the classical inferential problem of hypothesis testing through deep lear
case_studies.summary: The paper explores the application of deep learning to hypothesis testing, specifically dependence detection, by proposing a novel procedure called deep-testing. This approach leverages neural networks to distinguish between samples generated under a given statistical model and those generated outside that model. The outcome of this research could potentially lead to more effective statistical inference in various fields.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept, AI practitioners can experiment with using neural networks to classify samples as either conforming to or deviating from a specified statistical model. By doing so, they can develop novel statistical tests that leverage the strengths of deep learning, such as pattern recognition and robustness to noise.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity arising from this research could involve developing software or services that offer deep-testing capabilities for statistical analysis, targeting industries that heavily rely on data-driven decision-making. Companies could also use this technology to create more sophisticated analytics tools, enhancing their competitiveness in the market.

case_studies.title: Culturally Aware GenAI Risks for Youth: Perspectives from Youth, Parents, and Teachers in a Non-Western Context
case_studies.abstract: Generative AI tools are widely used by youth and have introduced new privacy and safety challenges. While prior research has explored youth's safety in GenAI within western context, it often overlooks the cultural, religious, and social dimensions of technology use that strongly shape youths digital experiences in countries like Saudi Arabia. To address the gap, this study explores children (aged 7 to 17), parents and teachers interactions with GenAI tools and risk perceptions through non-western lens. Through a mixed methods approach, we analyzed 736 Reddit and 1,262 X(Twitter) posts and cond
case_studies.summary: The problem of ensuring youth safety while using GenAI tools is a growing concern, particularly in non-Western contexts where cultural and social dimensions play a significant role. This study explores the interactions of children, parents, and teachers with GenAI tools and their risk perceptions through a non-Western lens using a mixed methods approach. The outcome of this study provides valuable insights into the cultural, religious, and social dimensions of technology use that shape youths' digital experiences in countries like Saudi Arabia.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the findings of this study by considering the cultural and social context of their target audience when developing and implementing GenAI tools, particularly in non-Western contexts. This can be achieved by conducting thorough user research and incorporating diverse perspectives into the design and development process to ensure that the tools are safe and effective for all users.
case_studies.monetisation: The insights gained from this study can be used to develop culturally sensitive GenAI tools that cater to the needs of youth in non-Western contexts, presenting a potential business opportunity for companies that specialize in AI-powered education or child safety. By addressing the concerns of parents, teachers, and youth in these contexts, companies can create products that are tailored to their needs, increasing the potential for adoption and revenue growth.

case_studies.title: Calibrated Surprise: An Information-Theoretic Account of Creative Quality
case_studies.abstract: The essence of good creative writing is calibrated surprise: when constraints from all relevant dimensions act together, the feasible solution space collapses into a narrow region, and the surviving choices look least predictable from an unconstrained view. "Calibrated" has a precise meaning: the author's intent, the reader's reasonable expectation, and the logic of reality converge. When these three independent judgements agree on every dimension, the set of admissible writing choices is forced into a very small region. A mathematical corollary follows: full-dimensional accuracy and mediocrit
case_studies.summary: The problem of evaluating creative writing quality is addressed through the concept of calibrated surprise, where constraints from multiple dimensions converge to produce a narrow range of feasible solutions. The AI approach involves developing a mathematical framework to quantify and predict the creative quality of writing based on information-theoretic principles. The outcome is a theoretical foundation for understanding and potentially generating high-quality creative writing, with potential applications in natural language processing and artificial intelligence.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the concept of calibrated surprise by incorporating multiple constraints and dimensions into their models to generate more creative and cohesive text. By using information-theoretic principles, practitioners can develop more sophisticated language models that balance predictability and surprise to produce high-quality writing.
case_studies.monetisation: The concept of calibrated surprise can be monetized through the development of AI-powered writing tools that help authors and content creators generate high-quality, engaging text. Such tools could be sold as software-as-a-service (SaaS) products or integrated into existing writing platforms, providing a concrete business opportunity for companies operating in the NLP and AI spaces.
